last_assistant_message:
**[Rigby]: Skill updated. Tested against the actual real staged file — found a genuine gap in my first test method, then a real corroborating line that validates the heuristic properly.**

**Changes to `skills/plaud-speaker-id/SKILL.md`** (additive, existing gate and heuristics 1-4/old-5/old-6 untouched, just renumbered where a new one landed in the middle):

- **New heuristic 5 — title self-identification matching.** Scans `sample_text` and other segments for the same speaker for self-identifying role language, cross-references against real attendee titles, and explicitly calls out that Plaud mangles spoken titles ("Chief County Officer" → "Chief Commercial Officer") — treat a phonetically/structurally close match to exactly one attendee as auto-resolvable. On par with (old) heuristic 5, now 6.
- **Heuristic 7 (was 6) — Clay-first, web-search fallback.** Explicit instruction: when Clay has no title/role data (recently-appointed leadership is exactly this case), fall back to a web search for the person's title at their employer, derived from their email domain.
- **Step 2b — domain capture.** Attendee extraction now captures each attendee's email domain alongside their name, not just the name.
- **Controller-prompt template** — updated to show `[title]` next to a name when heuristic 7 found one, and a conditional domain-mismatch callout ("R Jones — ashfordinc.com, different domain than the rest...") when at least one attendee's domain actually differs — explicitly not padded into every prompt.
- Added `WebSearch` to `.claude/skills/plaud-speaker-id/SKILL.md`'s `allowed-tools` — the new fallback needs it and it wasn't granted before.

**Tested against the real staged file, not synthetic data:** `~/Downloads/transcript-staging/plaud_08-25 Meeting_..._speakers.json` — confirmed `status: needs_mapping`, unanswered. Speaker 1's `sample_text` is exactly `"Chief County Officer."` (33 segments).

First pass, I scripted a naive character-similarity match between that fragment and the five real attendee titles (Ben Perelmuter/CEO, Jason Kreul/COO, Cory Chambers/CCO, Keith Oltchick/CDO, Nicole Shanks/CHRO) — it did **not** cleanly separate Cory Chambers from the field (crude string-overlap isn't phonetic similarity, and I want to report that honestly rather than claim a clean win off a flawed proxy).

So I pulled the actual full transcript (`.md`, same staging folder) for every Speaker 1 line — the heuristic as written explicitly says to check "other segments for that speaker, if the sample alone is inconclusive," and this is exactly why. At `[46:14]`, Speaker 1 says: *"...what agentic operations could be for operations and **commercial** on the phone and back office, so like accounting, finance **that's my world**."* That's an explicit, unambiguous self-identification with the commercial domain — nothing else in the transcript ties any other speaker to "commercial" — which corroborates the mis-transcribed title fragment and gives Knox (applying heuristic 5 as an LLM, not a lookup table) a clean, auto-resolvable path to Cory Chambers, matching your manual conclusion.

**Net result:** the new heuristic 5 is validated against the real recording it was written for — Speaker 1 → Cory Chambers would auto-resolve without a controller question, provided heuristic 7's web-search fallback actually surfaces "Chief Commercial Officer" for Cory Chambers (which it did, per your manual resolution tonight). I did not attempt to re-resolve Speakers 3/5/7 in this same recording — out of scope of what was asked, and I don't have enough corroborating transcript evidence for those in hand to make the same claim honestly.

Not committed. This is a separate, standalone change from the eval-hook-lifecycle work — I did not add it to `evolutions/.pending-changes.json`'s existing entry; let me know if you want it tracked as its own pending-changes item before packaging.
